content:
Hi all — sharing a small formalization project that might be of interest.

Repo: https://github.com/illyar80/p_vs_np

Formalizes the hook length formula for two families of Young diagrams via elementary Finset zone decomposition (no measure theory, no probability):

  • Hook shapes λ = (a+1, 1^l): product of hooks = (a+l+1)·a!·l!, dim V_λ = C(a+l, a)
  • Two-row diagrams λ = (a, b): product of hooks = descFac(a+1,b)·(a−b)!·b!, multiplication-form ballot identity

Also includes a formal bridge to Mathlib's YoungDiagram proving both representations (ρ, ℓ : ℕ → ℕ vs cells : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) compute identical hook lengths on valid cells.

Context: This is independent verification of two special cases already covered by the general result in NoahW314/KostkaNumbers (GNW hook walk). The value is the alternative proof method (FRT induction / product decomposition vs probabilistic hook walk) and explicit closed-form factorizations absent as named lemmas in the existing formalization. The general theorem is already proved — this project does not fill a gap.

Stats: 582 lines, zero sorry, zero substantive axioms (all verified via #print axioms — only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).

Frozen as of 2026-07-27. Feedback welcome.
Can you state the level of AI usage in this project?

This project was developed through iterative dialogue with an AI assistant (Claude) — it wrote the Lean code and proof strategies, I verified every step against lake build and #print axioms rather than taking claims at face value. Every theorem's axiom dependencies are documented in the README; the two places with substantive axioms (Test.lean, BIP.lean Part B) are explicitly separated from the sorry-free, zero-axiom modules. There was at least one caught error where an AI-derived formula was wrong (a hook-shape dimension miscalculation) and was corrected by hand-checking small cases before coding. Happy to answer specifics about any particular file/theorem.
This topic was moved here from #general > Hook length formula for special Young diagram families by Kevin Buzzard.
